title: Wake deliverable timer VI on a physical edge
description: Issues one local physical self-IPI after publishing HCR.VI only on the false-to-true edge of a priority-deliverable Pending INTID 17 or 18.
reason: EXP040 proved that LR state and HCR.VI remain correct while Apple cores stay in the Windows idle path; each external physical IPI caused fresh timer IAR and EOI activity and guest progress.
problem_fixed: A synthetic VI transition alone does not reliably wake a J313 core from the guest WFI path so a correctly pending Windows architectural timer can remain unconsumed indefinitely.
reproduction: Boot EXP040 and capture byte-identical frames with Pending INTID 18 and HCR.VI asserted; request one diagnostic physical IPI and observe timer acknowledgement and framebuffer progress.
implementation: Scans deliverable Pending LRs for architectural timer INTIDs; after setting HCR.VI performs ISB then sends one local IPI only when the previous VI value was clear; Active+Pending and repeated asserted VI states do not kick.
verification: The helper test first failed to compile and the integration contract failed before production code; afterward focused 49/49 complete nested host tests and complete root 258/258 passed with clean diff checks.
hardware_result: EXP041 reached runtime but froze at the disk-check countdown; physical IPI receive counts then grew by about 18000 per CPU with no virtual IAR/EOI progress because the fast FIQ path acknowledged each self-IPI before guest ERET.
notes: The timer-edge classification is retained as evidence but immediate emission is superseded; defer any physical kick until the final EL2-to-guest return boundary.

title: Defer timer wake until guest return
description: Latches the existing deliverable timer VI edge and emits its local physical IPI only after the final local-source drain and hv_exc_exit on the FIQ path.
reason: EXP041 showed that immediate self-IPI delivery was acknowledged by hv_handle_local_ipi in the same EL2 exception before ERET; physical IPI counts grew while Windows virtual IAR/EOI remained frozen.
problem_fixed: The intended physical wake never remained pending at the EL2-to-guest boundary so it could not wake the guest after ERET.
reproduction: Boot EXP041 at the disk-check freeze and compare two snapshots; observe approximately 18000 new physical IPIs per active CPU with unchanged virtual IAR/EOI counters.
implementation: Replaced the immediate send with a cacheline-separated per-CPU deferred flag; the final FIQ path flushes it after hv_exc_exit and performs ISB before the local IPI.
verification: The ordering contract failed on the missing flush before implementation; afterward vGIC/platform suites passed 37/37 complete nested host tests passed and complete root tests passed 258/258 with clean diff checks.
hardware_result: EXP042 advanced one disk-check phase but froze again; CPU1 and CPU5 each received over 25000 deferred physical IPIs while virtual IAR/EOI remained unchanged because the HCR-derived edge repeatedly re-armed for the same Pending timer.
notes: Deferred placement is correct and retained; replace only HCR-bit edge identity with one latch per continuous deliverable Pending timer interval.

title: Latch one wake per deliverable Pending timer interval
description: Tracks per-CPU timer deliverability independently of HCR.VI and defers exactly one physical wake when a Pending INTID 17 or 18 first becomes priority-deliverable; the latch resets when that condition ends.
reason: EXP042 proved deferred placement but measured more than 25000 physical IPIs with unchanged virtual IAR/EOI because HCR.VI transitions do not identify one timer delivery lifecycle.
problem_fixed: Repeated physical FIQs for the same unconsumed Pending timer can starve the guest and recreate the apparent freeze the wake was intended to resolve.
reproduction: Boot EXP042 and compare snapshots around the static disk-check frame; CPU1 IPI rises 22065 to 48374 while IAR/EOI stays 14516 and CPU5 rises 19961 to 45404 while IAR/EOI stays 9286.
implementation: Added a tested two-state deliverability transition and cacheline-separated per-CPU latch; continuous deliverability suppresses repeat wakes and masking IAR or removal resets the interval while preserving the deferred FIQ-return send.
verification: The host state-transition test and root source contract failed before implementation; afterward vGIC/platform suites passed 37/37 complete nested host tests passed complete root tests passed 258/258 and diff checks passed.
hardware_result: EXP043 autonomously passed both former freeze frames and eliminated the repeated physical IPI storm but Windows later bugchecked with 0x133 P1=1 for cumulative time at IRQL DISPATCH_LEVEL or above; the final snapshot had no pending timer LR on CPUs 1 through 7.
notes: Do not retain as a stable fix or make a fourth incremental wake patch; collect the new Windows dump and perform an architectural A/B against the accepted 2026-08-13 contract.

title: Make trapped idle timer delivery deterministic
description: Makes HCR TWI and TWE plus the WFI/WFE exception path unconditional; keeps the proven live CNTV level-to-LR synchronization and removes the entire experimental physical timer self-IPI path.
reason: EXP044 measured frozen cores sleeping without TWI/TWE; EXP045 proved trapping alone reaches EL2 but leaves asserted Active timer LRs stale; EXP040 proved the complementary Active-to-Active+Pending level correction; EXP041 through EXP043 rejected physical self-IPIs.
problem_fixed: An idle Windows vCPU could sleep past a deliverable virtual timer or receive disruptive physical self-IPIs while the hypervisor failed to preserve the architectural level state in its live LR.
reproduction: Boot EXP044 to reproduce missing HCR bits and Active-only expired timers; boot EXP045 to reproduce the same stale LR with traps enabled; boot EXP043 to reproduce the 0x133 P1=1 self-IPI outcome.
implementation: Applies and verifies TWI/TWE on initial guarded HCR preflight secondary restore and every runtime whole-HCR write; handles trapped WFI/WFE in all profiles; removes timer wake latch deferred flush and physical self-IPI emission while retaining CNTV asserted/deasserted live-LR synchronization.
verification: RED source contracts failed on the optional flag and self-IPI path; focused timer WFX and vGIC tests passed; complete nested host suite passed; complete root suite passed 258/258; clean APPLE_INPUT=0 freestanding build passed; diff checks passed.

title: Trap idle only for a pending virtual IRQ
description: Couples HCR TWI and TWE exactly to HCR.VI so ordinary guest WFI/WFE retains architectural sleep while a vCPU cannot sleep again after a virtual interrupt becomes deliverable.
reason: EXP046 proved that permanently trapping idle creates a tight return regime with Pending timer LRs and unchanged virtual IAR/EOI; EXP040 proved a physical boundary can wake ordinary WFI and the existing host timer already provides that boundary.
problem_fixed: The static trap distorted every idle cycle while the no-trap path could return an awakened vCPU to sleep despite a newly published VI.
reproduction: Boot EXP046 and compare two snapshots more than 30 seconds apart; observe Pending INTID 18 plus HCR.VI and invariant IAR/EOI on all affected vCPUs while host ticks continue.
implementation: The whole-HCR policy helper now sets TWI/TWE only when the same value contains VI and clears them otherwise; initial and secondary HCR preserve normal idle; the existing WFI/WFE handler remains available only for the pending-VI window; no IPI timer LR or cadence behavior changed.
verification: RED helper and root source contracts failed before implementation; focused WFX timer and vGIC tests passed; complete nested host suite passed; complete root suite passed 258/258; clean APPLE_INPUT=0 freestanding build passed; diff checks passed.
hardware_result: All eight vCPUs plus NVMe and xHCI reached runtime, but two snapshots over 30 seconds apart showed Pending deliverable INTID 18 with VI plus TWI/TWE and unchanged virtual IAR/EOI; the framebuffer remained black and TCP/22 never appeared.
notes: Dynamic trapping obeys its contract but cannot wake an already sleeping Apple core; restore the separately validated one-shot physical doorbell and diagnose the later 0x133 independently.

title: Restore one deferred timer doorbell per deliverable interval

verification: RED pure helper and integration contracts failed first; focused and complete nested suites passed; complete public suite passed 258/258; strict artifact preflight passed.
hardware_result: EXP048 passed the prior black frame and reached lock screen, but two snapshots measured hundreds of thousands of excess physical IPIs and the guest remained intermittently frozen; Stage1 recovered.

title: Emulate trapped guest idle with a real EL2 wait

verification: RED WFx and source-contract tests failed first; focused suites and complete nested tests passed; complete public suite passed 258/258; clean freestanding build and strict manifest preflight passed.
hardware_result: EXP049 eliminated all excess timer self-IPIs so physical IPI counts exactly matched ordinary SGI queues, but the framebuffer stayed black for more than 90 seconds and TCP/22 never appeared; Stage1 recovered.

title: Add bounded J313 Apple input MMIO primitives
description: Implemented the inert Windows-side SPI3 and GPIO primitives required for native Apple SPI HID transport without invoking them from device power callbacks.

title: Add bounded passive Apple input transport diagnostics
description: Connected APPL0001 to a passive KMDF interrupt worker that drains at most 32 Apple SPI HID packets and exposes a versioned read-only diagnostic snapshot plus ARM64 and KD clients.
